title: Introduction to CNNs: Understanding Deep Learning for Computer Vision

cues.en: Instructor: Hello, and welcome back to the course on deep learning.
cues.zh: 大家好，歡迎回到深度學習課程。

cues.en: Today, we're kicking off convolutional neural networks.
cues.zh: 今天要開始卷積神經網路。

cues.en: This is gonna be exciting. Let's dive straight into it.
cues.zh: 這會很精彩，直接開始吧。

cues.en: We're going to start off with an image.
cues.zh: 先從一張圖片開始。

cues.en: What do you see when you look at this image?
cues.zh: 看這張圖，你看到了什麼？

cues.en: Do you see a person looking at you?
cues.zh: 是一個看著你的人嗎？

cues.en: Or do you see a person looking to the right?
cues.zh: 還是一個向右看的人？

cues.en: You can see that your brain is struggling.
cues.zh: 你會發現大腦正在掙扎。

cues.en: It's struggling to adjust.
cues.zh: 它努力在調整判斷。

cues.en: If you look to the right side of the image, just look at the right border of the image, you'll see a person looking to the right.
cues.zh: 看圖片右側，只看右邊緣，就會看到一個向右看的人。

cues.en: If you look at the left border of the image, you'll see a person looking at you.
cues.zh: 看圖片左邊緣，則會看到一個看著你的人。

cues.en: And this just proves that what our brain is looking for when we see things is features.
cues.zh: 這說明了，我們看東西時，大腦尋找的是特徵。

cues.en: Depending on the features that it sees, depending on the features that you process, you categorize things in certain ways.
cues.zh: 根據看到、處理到的特徵，你會用不同方式將事物分類。

cues.en: So when you look on the right side of the image, you see certain features of a person looking to the right because they're closer to your center of focus, and therefore your brain classifies it
cues.zh: 看右側時，你會看到向右看的人的某些特徵，因為它們比較靠近視線焦點，所以大腦把它判斷為

cues.en: as a person looking to the right.
cues.zh: 一個向右看的人。

cues.en: When you look to the left side of the image, you see more features of a person looking at you, and therefore your brain classifies it as such.
cues.zh: 看左側時，則看到更多朝你看的人的特徵，因此大腦就做出那樣的判斷。

cues.en: So let's have a look at another one.
cues.zh: 再看另一張。

cues.en: This is a very famous image.
cues.zh: 這張圖非常有名。

cues.en: You probably have already seen it.
cues.zh: 你可能已經看過。

cues.en: But what do you see here?
cues.zh: 這裡你看到了什麼？

cues.en: So some people will say that they see a young lady wearing a dress, looking away.
cues.zh: 有人會說，看到穿著洋裝、轉頭看向別處的年輕女子。

cues.en: Some people will say they see an old lady wearing a scarf on her head, looking down.
cues.zh: 有人則會說，看到頭戴圍巾、低頭看的老婦人。

cues.en: So I'm gonna point these features out, and you'll see that it'll become very obvious.
cues.zh: 我來指出這些特徵，你就會覺得很明顯了。

cues.en: So this is the face of the young lady looking away.
cues.zh: 這是轉頭看向別處的年輕女子的臉。

cues.en: She's looking into the distance.
cues.zh: 她正望向遠方。

cues.en: That's her coat, that's her hair, that's her little feather in her hair.
cues.zh: 這是外套、頭髮，以及頭髮上的小羽毛。

cues.en: And on the other hand, this is the head of the old lady looking down.
cues.zh: 另一方面，這是低著頭的老婦人的頭部。

cues.en: That's her nose, that's her mouth, that's her chin, that's the scarf on her head, and she's looking down.
cues.zh: 這是鼻子、嘴巴、下巴和頭上的圍巾，她正低著頭。

cues.en: So as you can see, two in one, and depending on which features your brain picks up, it will switch between classifying the image
cues.zh: 同一張圖有兩種解讀。根據大腦捕捉到的特徵，影像的分類會切換，

cues.en: as one or the other.
cues.zh: 一下是這個，一下是另一個。

cues.en: The oldest one of these illusions recorded in the printed work is this one.
cues.zh: 在印刷作品中有紀錄的這類錯覺，最早的是這張。

cues.en: It's the duck or the rabbit.
cues.zh: 鴨子或兔子。

cues.en: So is this a duck, or is this a rabbit? Another example.
cues.zh: 這是鴨子還是兔子？又是一個例子。

cues.en: And now I'm gonna show you an image which will, just for a second, just look at it and see what emotions or what kind of visual experience you go through.
cues.zh: 再給你看一張圖。先看一秒，注意自己有什麼感受，或經歷什麼視覺體驗。

cues.en: So what do you see?
cues.zh: 你看到了什麼？

cues.en: Does you feel, like, a bit, not dizzy, but a bit dazzled, like your brain is trying to understand what it is, what it is?
cues.zh: 會不會覺得有點眼花，雖然不到頭暈，但大腦一直想弄清楚這是什麼？

cues.en: Like, it's jumping between her eyes, the up and down eyes.
cues.zh: 視線好像在她上下兩組眼睛之間跳動。

cues.en: And this is a classic example of when there are certain features where it could be this, it could be that, but your brain cannot decide
cues.zh: 這是典型例子：某些特徵可能代表這個，也可能代表那個，大腦卻無法決定，

cues.en: because both seem plausible.
cues.zh: 因為兩種解讀都合理。

cues.en: And yeah, so basically, all these examples illustrate to us how the brain works, that it processes certain features on an image or on whatever you see in real life,
cues.zh: 這些例子都在說明大腦如何運作：它會處理圖片或現實生活中所見的某些特徵，

cues.en: and it classifies that as such.
cues.zh: 然後據此分類。

cues.en: And you've probably been in situations when you look over your shoulder quickly and you see something.
cues.zh: 你可能也遇過，快速回頭時看見某樣東西，

cues.en: You think it's, I don't know, it's like a ball, but it turns out to be a cat.
cues.zh: 以為是球，結果卻是貓。

cues.en: Or you think it's a car, but it turns out to be a shadow and things like that.
cues.zh: 或以為是車子，結果只是影子之類的。

cues.en: That's because you don't have enough time to process those features or you don't have enough features to classify things as such.
cues.zh: 那是因為沒有足夠時間處理特徵，或沒有足夠特徵讓你正確分類。

cues.en: And for me, this is very interesting because what we're going to be doing with neural networks, with convolutional neural networks, is very similar,
cues.zh: 我覺得這很有趣，因為我們接下來使用神經網路，尤其是卷積神經網路時，做的事情很類似，

cues.en: and you'll find that the way that computers are going to be processing images is going to be extremely similar to the way we are processing images.
cues.zh: 你會發現，電腦處理影像的方式，和我們處理影像的方式非常相近。

cues.en: So it's very valuable to understand and just kind of remember these things, that this is how we do it.
cues.zh: 所以了解並記住我們是如何處理影像的，很有價值。

cues.en: And I'm going to take this lady off your screens because she's probably already freaking you out by now.
cues.zh: 先把這位女士從畫面移開，她可能已經讓你有點不舒服了。

cues.en: So here's something different.
cues.zh: 換點別的。

cues.en: Here's an experiment, an experiment done on computers, on convolutional neural networks, so we're slowly moving now from humans to computers,
cues.zh: 這是用電腦、用卷積神經網路做的實驗。我們慢慢從人類轉到電腦，

cues.en: and this slide is from a talk by Geoffrey Hinton.
cues.zh: 這張投影片來自 Geoffrey Hinton 的演講。

cues.en: And here, basically, it describes an experiment that he had done on some convolutional neural networks that he had trained up.
cues.zh: 它介紹了他用訓練好的卷積神經網路所做的實驗。

cues.en: So here, you see three images, and we're gonna go through them left to right and see how you would classify them and then see how the computer classified them.
cues.zh: 這裡有三張圖，我們由左到右看看，你會如何分類，再看電腦如何分類。

cues.en: So on the left, what do you think this is?
cues.zh: 左邊這張，你覺得是什麼？

cues.en: You probably said cheetah, and you'll be right, and this is what the computer said.
cues.zh: 你可能說是獵豹，沒錯，電腦也是這樣判斷。

cues.en: And right away, right off the bat, we're going to learn how to read these images because if you're going to go deep into convolutional neural networks, no pun intended,
cues.zh: 我們先學習怎麼讀這類圖表。因為如果要深入研究卷積神經網路，這裡可不是刻意玩「深度」的雙關，

cues.en: if you're going to start learning more and more about them and using them, you'll see a lot of these, and I've actually seen people read them incorrectly.
cues.zh: 隨著學習與使用越來越深入，你會經常看到它們，而我真的看過有人解讀錯誤。

cues.en: So here at the top, a cheetah is what it actually is, so that's the actual correct label of the image.
cues.zh: 最上面的 cheetah 是它實際的類別，也就是這張影像的正確標籤。

cues.en: That's what the label of the image is, regardless of any processing and computer vision.
cues.zh: 無論是否經過電腦視覺處理，這都是影像本身的標籤。

cues.en: And then here are the guesses, the top four or five sometimes guesses of the algorithm, and they're given the probability.
cues.zh: 下方是演算法機率最高的四個，有時是五個猜測，以及對應機率。

cues.en: So the computer said, or the neural network said, cheetah, leopard, snow leopard, or Egyptian cat can be one of the four, and cheetah has the highest vote.
cues.zh: 神經網路認為可能是獵豹、豹、雪豹或埃及貓，其中獵豹的得票最高。

cues.en: And throughout this part of the course, you'll understand what these votes mean and how they are derived.
cues.zh: 在這個單元中，你會了解這些票數的意義，以及它們如何得出。

cues.en: But for now, it's pretty intuitive, right?
cues.zh: 目前看起來很直覺，對吧？

cues.en: So it's a cheetah in reality, and the neural network guessed right.
cues.zh: 實際上是獵豹，神經網路也猜對了。

cues.en: It said with a high probability about like 95, 99%, it's a cheetah.
cues.zh: 它認為大約有 95%、99% 這麼高的機率是獵豹。

cues.en: Then the second one, what do you think that is?
cues.zh: 第二張，你認為是什麼？

cues.en: That is a bullet train.
cues.zh: 這是高速列車。

cues.en: And the neural network was able to distinguish between bullet train, passenger car, subway train, electric locomotive.
cues.zh: 神經網路能區分高速列車、客車、地鐵列車和電力機車。

cues.en: Those are the top choices.
cues.zh: 這些是機率最高的選項。

cues.en: Of course it had many more options.
cues.zh: 當然，它原本有更多可能選項。

cues.en: These neural networks learn to distinguish from not just four categories, from dozens, thousands of categories at the same time.
cues.zh: 這類神經網路不只學會分四類，而是同時區分數十甚至數千種類別。

cues.en: So those are the four options that it picked, and so that's a bullet train, and it's a bullet train.
cues.zh: 這是它選出的四個選項；實際是高速列車，它也判斷為高速列車。

cues.en: So what do you think the last one is?
cues.zh: 最後一張，你覺得是什麼？

cues.en: There are a couple of options, right?
cues.zh: 有幾種可能，對吧？

cues.en: It's not very clear what it is.
cues.zh: 不太看得出來。

cues.en: It could be a frying pan, it could be a magnifying glass, it could be even maybe a pair of scissors, some might say.
cues.zh: 可能是平底鍋、放大鏡，有些人甚至會說是剪刀。

cues.en: Well, the neural network said it was a pair of scissors.
cues.zh: 神經網路判斷是剪刀。

cues.en: But you can see how you can go wrong here.
cues.zh: 不過你也看得出來，這裡為什麼容易判斷錯。

cues.en: First of all, it's not a very clear image.
cues.zh: 首先，影像本身不太清楚。

cues.en: And also, you can see that the probabilities are not as clear here, so the neural network was a bit confused, a bit indecisive, just as we are.
cues.zh: 而且各個機率也沒有明顯差距，神經網路和我們一樣，有點困惑、猶豫。

cues.en: So it said scissors was the highest probability, but then it had hand glass, which it actually was, with not so far away on the second place, it said frying pan, stethoscope.
cues.zh: 它認為剪刀機率最高，實際上的正解手持放大鏡排第二，差距不大，後面還有平底鍋和聽診器。

cues.en: So basically, here you can see that scissors was its first guess, but the correct option was number two, and that's why it's highlighted in red.
cues.zh: 也就是說，剪刀是第一個猜測，正確答案卻是第二個，所以用紅色標示。

cues.en: So there we go.
cues.zh: 就是這樣。

cues.en: That's what neural networks are already capable of.
cues.zh: 神經網路已經能做到這些事。

cues.en: And this is actually quite an old slide.
cues.zh: 而這其實是一張相當舊的投影片。

cues.en: This was several years ago.
cues.zh: 已經是幾年前的內容。

cues.en: Now they're even better, and you will see that from the practical application that you will be coding together.
cues.zh: 現在它們更厲害了，接下來一起寫程式做實際應用時，你就會看到。

cues.en: But now let's try and understand a bit better what ConvNets, or convolutional neural networks, actually are and why are they gaining so much popularity.
cues.zh: 先進一步了解 ConvNets，也就是卷積神經網路，到底是什麼，以及為什麼越來越受歡迎。

cues.en: And they actually are gaining popularity.
cues.zh: 它們確實越來越熱門。

cues.en: So you can see here a Google Trends comparison I did just yesterday.
cues.zh: 這裡是我昨天才做的 Google Trends 比較。

cues.en: Here, you can see that convolutional neural networks are even taking over artificial neural networks.
cues.zh: 可以看到，卷積神經網路的熱度甚至正在超越人工神經網路。

cues.en: So a massive increase, and they're just gonna keep going that way because it is a very important field.
cues.zh: 成長非常大，而且還會持續，因為這是很重要的領域。

cues.en: That is where all the things happen, such as, like, self-driving cars, how do they recognize people on the road, how do they recognize stop signs and things like that?
cues.zh: 例如自駕車如何辨識路上的行人、停止標誌等，都是這個領域的應用。

cues.en: How does Facebook, how is Facebook able to tag images, or people in images?
cues.zh: Facebook 又是如何標記影像，或影像中的人物？

cues.en: Like, remember previously, years ago, you had to tag people yourself?
cues.zh: 還記得幾年前，必須自己標記人物嗎？

cues.en: Then it would recognize faces, you had to add the names, and now it just recognizes the faces and adds the names at the same time.
cues.zh: 後來能辨識臉孔，但要自行加名字；現在辨識臉孔和加上名字可以同時完成。

cues.en: Well, that is what convolutional neural networks are capable of.
cues.zh: 這就是卷積神經網路能做到的事。

cues.en: And speaking of Facebook, if Geoffrey Hinton is the godfather of artificial neural networks and deep learning,
cues.zh: 說到 Facebook，如果 Geoffrey Hinton 是人工神經網路與深度學習的教父，

cues.en: then Yann LeCun is the grandfather of convolutional neural networks.
cues.zh: 那 Yann LeCun 就是卷積神經網路的祖父。

cues.en: Yann LeCun is a student of Geoffrey Hinton's.
cues.zh: Yann LeCun 是 Geoffrey Hinton 的學生。

cues.en: And in fact, here, you can see them together.
cues.zh: 這裡可以看到他們的合照。

cues.en: And Geoffrey Hinton now is pioneering deep learning at Google.
cues.zh: Geoffrey Hinton 現在正於 Google 開拓深度學習。

cues.en: Yann LeCun is the director of Facebook artificial intelligence research and also a professor at NYU.
cues.zh: Yann LeCun 是 Facebook 人工智慧研究的主管，同時也是紐約大學教授。

cues.en: So I love this part of the course.
cues.zh: 我很喜歡課程這個部分。

cues.en: Slowly we're building up these names or this kind of picture of the profiles of the people who are driving this field,
cues.zh: 我們逐漸認識這些名字，建立起推動這個領域的人物輪廓，

cues.en: and in the next couple of parts, we'll get to know about a few more, and we'll have this whole mafia, as they call themselves, or Yann LeCun calls them,
cues.zh: 接下來幾個部分還會認識更多人，逐漸了解他們自稱，或 Yann LeCun 所稱的這群黑手黨，

cues.en: mafia or conspiracy of deep learning, and you'll learn a bit more about how this whole field developed.
cues.zh: 也就是深度學習的黑手黨或共謀者，並更了解這個領域的發展。

cues.en: And yeah, these are just some great, great people.
cues.zh: 他們都是很了不起的人。

cues.en: And so Yann LeCun, back in the '80s and the '90s, made significant contributions to the field of convolutional neural networks
cues.zh: Yann LeCun 在 1980、1990 年代，對卷積神經網路領域做出了重大貢獻，

cues.en: and, as we'll see throughout this course, has been able to develop or help the world develop something so extremely powerful.
cues.zh: 如同課程接下來會看到的，他開發，或協助世界開發出極為強大的技術。

cues.en: So moving on to how convolutional neural networks work.
cues.zh: 接著談卷積神經網路如何運作。

cues.en: You have an input.
cues.zh: 先有輸入。

cues.en: It's very simple, it's very straightforward.
cues.zh: 很簡單、很直接。

cues.en: So you have an input image, it goes through the convolutional neural network, and you have an output label, so it classifies that image as something,
cues.zh: 輸入一張影像，通過卷積神經網路，再輸出一個標籤，把影像分類為某個類別，

cues.en: like as a cheetah or a bullet train or something else.
cues.zh: 例如獵豹、高速列車或其他東西。

cues.en: Now, kind of like going into a bit more detail, for instance, after a neural network has been trained up,
cues.zh: 再深入一點，神經網路完成訓練後，

cues.en: on certain images, on certain classified images or categorized images that have been categorized prior, after that, you can give it,
cues.zh: 也就是用一些事先已分類、標註好類別的影像訓練之後，你就可以給它新的影像。

cues.en: let's say a neural network has been trained up to recognize facial expressions, emotions.
cues.zh: 假設網路已訓練成能辨識臉部表情與情緒。

cues.en: You can give it a face of a smiling person, not just a face like a drawing of a face like this, but actual face of a person smiling, and it will tell you that that person is happy.
cues.zh: 給它一張微笑的人臉，這裡指的是真人微笑的臉，不只是這樣畫出來的臉，它就會告訴你這個人很開心。

cues.en: And you can give it a face of a person that's frowning.
cues.zh: 也可以給它皺眉的人臉。

cues.en: It will tell you that the person is sad.
cues.zh: 它會告訴你這個人很難過。

cues.en: It can recognize these emotions.
cues.zh: 它能辨識這些情緒。

cues.en: And as you can see, that's already very powerful in terms of so many different applications just of this one example you can think of right away.
cues.zh: 光這個例子，你可能立刻就想到很多應用，可見它已經非常強大。

cues.en: And in both cases, it will give you a probability, so it won't say, you know, with 100%, the person's happy or sad.
cues.zh: 兩種情況都會給出機率，不會百分之百斷言這個人開心或難過。

cues.en: It'll be 99 or 98 or maybe 80% when it's unclear of what's going on.
cues.zh: 可能是 99%、98%，如果不太清楚，也可能是 80%。

cues.en: And just like we are, right, sometimes we can mistake things for what they're not, or sometimes it's just not clear if the person is smiling or frowning
cues.zh: 就像我們有時會認錯，有時不確定對方是在微笑還是皺眉，

cues.en: or if it's a dog or a cat or if it's a train or a bullet train, right?
cues.zh: 或不確定是狗還是貓、一般列車還是高速列車。

cues.en: Sometimes we haven't seen enough features.
cues.zh: 有時只是還沒看見足夠特徵。

cues.en: And it all goes down to features because that's how we process visual information, as we saw from the start of this tutorial.
cues.zh: 一切都回到特徵，因為如同本堂開頭所見，我們就是這樣處理視覺資訊的。

cues.en: But how does a neural network...
cues.zh: 但神經網路是怎麼……

cues.en: How is a neural network able to recognize these features?
cues.zh: 神經網路如何辨識這些特徵？

cues.en: Well, it all starts at the very basic level.
cues.zh: 一切都從最基本的層次開始。

cues.en: Let's say you have an image, you have two images.
cues.zh: 假設有兩張影像。

cues.en: One is a black-and-white image of two-by-two pixels, and one is a colored image of two-by-two pixels.
cues.zh: 一張是 2 × 2 像素的黑白影像，另一張是 2 × 2 像素的彩色影像。

cues.en: Well, neural networks leverage the fact that the black-and-white image is a two-dimensional, like, array.
cues.zh: 神經網路利用了黑白影像本質上是二維陣列的特性。

cues.en: So the way we see it right now on the left is just the visual representation, right?
cues.zh: 左邊現在看到的只是視覺呈現，對吧？

cues.en: So it's some kind of picture, and for simplicity's sake, it's just a two-by-two picture.
cues.zh: 為了簡化，它只是一張 2 × 2 的圖片。

cues.en: But in computer terms, it's actually a two-dimensional array with every single one of those pixels having a value between 0 and 255.
cues.zh: 但對電腦而言，它是二維陣列，每個像素都有一個介於 0 到 255 的值。

cues.en: So that's eight bits of information, 2 to the power of 8 is 256, so therefore the values are from 0 to 255, and that's the intensity of the color,
cues.zh: 這是 8 位元資訊，2 的 8 次方是 256，因此數值從 0 到 255，代表顏色強度，

cues.en: and in this case, the color white.
cues.zh: 這裡是白色的強度。

cues.en: So 0 will be a completely black pixel, 255 will be a completely white pixel, and between them, you have the grayscale range of possible options for this pixel.
cues.zh: 0 表示全黑像素，255 表示全白，兩者之間則是這個像素可能的灰階值。

cues.en: And based on that information, computers are able to then work with the image.
cues.zh: 電腦就能根據這些資訊處理影像。

cues.en: And that's kind of like the starting point, that any image actually has a digital representation, has a digital form, and those are just basically ones and zeros
cues.zh: 這就是起點：任何影像都有數位表示形式，基本上是用 0 和 1，

cues.en: that form a number 0 to 255 for every single pixel.
cues.zh: 為每個像素組成 0 到 255 的數字。

cues.en: And that's what the computer works with.
cues.zh: 電腦處理的就是這些。

cues.en: It doesn't actually work with, you know, the colors or anything.
cues.zh: 它其實不是直接處理顏色之類的東西。

cues.en: It works with the ones and zeros at the end of the day.
cues.zh: 歸根究柢，它處理的是 0 和 1。

cues.en: That's kind of like the foundation of it all.
cues.zh: 這是整件事的基礎。

cues.en: And in a colored image, it's actually a three-dimensional array.
cues.zh: 彩色影像則是三維陣列。

cues.en: You've got a blue pixel...
cues.zh: 有藍色像素……

cues.en: You've got a blue layer, a green layer, and a red layer, and that stands for RGB, red, green, blue, and each one of those colors has its own intensity.
cues.zh: 有藍色層、綠色層和紅色層，也就是 RGB：紅、綠、藍，每個顏色都有自己的強度。

cues.en: So basically, a pixel has three values assigned to it, each one of them is between 0 and 255,
cues.zh: 所以每個像素都對應三個值，各自介於 0 到 255，

cues.en: and therefore you can find out what's this image, what color exactly this pixel is by combining those three values.
cues.zh: 把這三個值組合起來，就能知道影像中這個像素確切是什麼顏色。

cues.en: And again, computers are going to be working with that.
cues.zh: 電腦同樣會處理這些數值。

cues.en: So that's the foundation of it all.
cues.zh: 這就是基本原理。

cues.en: That's the red channel, the green channel, the blue channel.
cues.zh: 這是紅色通道、綠色通道和藍色通道。

cues.en: And finally, let's have a look at, for instance, an example, a very trivial example of a smiling face.
cues.zh: 最後再看一個非常簡單的笑臉範例。

cues.en: In computer terms, if we just really simplify things, instead of having from 0 to 255, instead of having those values, just so that we can understand things better
cues.zh: 從電腦的角度，為了讓概念更容易理解，我們不使用 0 到 255 的值，而是極度簡化，

cues.en: and really grasp the concepts, we're going to say 0 is white, 1 is black, right?
cues.zh: 改成 0 是白色、1 是黑色。

cues.en: So we're just going to simplify things to the extreme, and you'll see that that image can be represented like that.
cues.zh: 如此大幅簡化後，你會看到這張影像可以這樣表示。

cues.en: So the reason why we've brought this up is because we're going to, all of our tutorials, we're going to structure on images like this, which are very simple, but at the same time, then all of those concepts
cues.zh: 之所以介紹這個，是因為接下來所有教學都會用這種簡單影像說明，而這些概念

cues.en: can translate back to the 0 to 256 range of values, and everything applies the same way there.
cues.zh: 也都能套回 0 到 256 的數值範圍，運作方式相同。

cues.en: And the steps that we're going to be going through with these images are step number one, convolution, step number two, max pooling, step number three, flattening, and step number four, full connection.
cues.zh: 處理影像會依序經過第一步卷積、第二步最大池化、第三步攤平，以及第四步全連接。

cues.en: And I can imagine that probably none of these words mean much to you at the moment, but by the end of this section of the course, you will understand them in great detail
cues.zh: 你現在可能還不太了解這些名詞，但本章結束時，就會非常清楚它們的細節，

cues.en: and exactly what they're doing.
cues.zh: 以及各自到底在做什麼。

cues.en: So we'll get started on the next tutorial.
cues.zh: 下一堂教學就正式開始。

cues.en: For now, the additional reading that you might want to look into is Yann LeCun's original paper
cues.zh: 目前可以先閱讀 Yann LeCun 的原始論文，

cues.en: that gave the rise to convolutional neural networks.
cues.zh: 這篇論文促成了卷積神經網路的發展。

cues.en: It's called Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition.
cues.zh: 標題是 Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition。

cues.en: You may have seen this image before floating around the internet.
cues.zh: 你可能在網路上看過這張圖。

cues.en: It is from that paper.
cues.zh: 它就出自那篇論文。

cues.en: So if you wanna go back to the very beginnings of how it all happened, where it all came from, this is the paper to look into.
cues.zh: 如果想追溯這一切最初如何發生、從何而來，就可以讀這篇論文。

cues.en: And I look forward to seeing you on the next tutorial.
cues.zh: 期待下一堂教學與你見面。

cues.en: Until then, enjoy deep learning.
cues.zh: 在那之前，祝你享受深度學習的樂趣。
